hints: Notice that yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine means a positive tri-iodomethane (iodoform) test, so look for a specific group in the molecule.
Use the 66.7% carbon by mass and one oxygen per molecule to work out the molar mass, it points to a formula with four carbons and one oxygen.
Check which of the C4H8O isomers contains a CH3CO group that can be oxidised to give CHI3, and which one cannot.
walkthrough:
**Decode the iodoform test**

Great start, that yellow precipitate is the classic clue. It tells you T gives a positive tri-iodomethane test.

That only happens if T has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group (methyl ketone) or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group (which is oxidised in situ to the methyl ketone).

**Use the % carbon to find the formula**

Now let's use the numbers. T has one O atom per molecule, so mass of O = 16.

Let $M_r$ be the molar mass of T:
$$\frac{\text{mass of C}}{M_r} \times 100 = 66.7$$
If T has 4 carbon atoms, mass of C = $4 \times 12 = 48$:
$$M_r = \frac{48 \times 100}{66.7} \approx 72$$
This fits perfectly: $48 + 16 = 64$, leaving 8 for H, so $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$.

**Test the options against both clues**

Both butanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) and butanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) have formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$, so both fit the % C clue.

But only butanone has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group needed for the iodoform reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Butanal has $\text{-CHO}$ but not $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so it is negative. Therefore T must be butanone.

options.A: Incorrect. Methylpropan-2-ol is $(CH_3)_3COH$ with formula $C_4H_{10}O$ ($M_r = 74$). Its % C is about 64.9%, not 66.7%, and as a tertiary alcohol with no $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group it gives a negative iodoform test.
options.B: Incorrect. Butan-2-ol, $CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3$, does give a positive iodoform test because of its $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group, which is a tempting trap. However its formula is $C_4H_{10}O$ ($M_r = 74$), giving about 64.9% C, so it fails the percentage clue.
options.C: Incorrect. Butanal, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CHO$, has the correct formula $C_4H_8O$ and correct 66.7% C, but it lacks a $CH_3CO-$ group. Only ethanal gives a positive iodoform test among aldehydes, so butanal gives no yellow precipitate.
options.D: Correct. Butanone, $CH_3COCH_2CH_3$, has formula $C_4H_8O$ ($M_r = 72$) giving $48/72 \times 100 = 66.7$% C. It is a methyl ketone with a $CH_3CO-$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform test with yellow $CHI_3$ precipitate.
